title: Physics
summary: A rigorous three-year independent-study pathway spanning mathematical methods, classical mechanics, electromagnetism, waves and optics, relativity, quantum mechanics, thermodynamics and statistical physics, scientific computing and inference, experimental physics, research communication, one coherent depth concentration, and a defended senior research thesis.
notice: Course Atlas is not a university, physics department, or accreditor. It awards no degree, diploma, academic credit, transfer credit, laboratory authorization, research appointment, or guaranteed provider certificate. This disciplinary pathway does not reproduce a university's general education, supervised facilities, faculty mentorship, peer research culture, or institutional credential. Completion evidence is a self-directed portfolio that another person may evaluate independently.
workload: Every course carries 4 Course Atlas credits and 160 nominal hours: eight ordered units of about 20 hours each. Unit numbers express sequence, not fixed calendar weeks. The completion contract is 30 courses and 120 Course Atlas credits, approximately 4,800 hours. A standard term is 20 weeks with five concurrent courses at roughly 40 hours per week; learners may slow the calendar without changing requirements. When safe supervised laboratory access is unavailable, a rigorously verified simulation, remote instrument, or open-data investigation may satisfy the portfolio evidence contract, but it does not grant authorization to use radiation, lasers, cryogens, vacuum, high voltage, or other controlled equipment.
outcomes: Use calculus, linear algebra, differential equations, complex methods, symmetry, and approximation to formulate and test physical models.
Reason across classical mechanics, fields, waves, optics, relativity, quantum theory, thermodynamics, statistical physics, matter, nuclei, particles, and the cosmos.
Plan safe experiments or defensible simulation and open-data alternatives, calibrate evidence, quantify uncertainty, and diagnose systematic error.
Build reproducible numerical models and inference pipelines whose stability, convergence, provenance, and limitations are explicit.
Read scientific literature critically and communicate responsible claims in notebooks, papers, visualizations, talks, and oral examinations.
Formulate, execute, document, and publicly defend a substantial independent Physics research project.
